heroHeadline: Day 1085: NYT Reveals Netanyahu Never Told Security Chiefs of UAE's October 7 Warning at Oct. 1, 2023 Meeting, as IDF Probe Finds Paga Outpost Unprepared for the Attack
heroSubtitle: The deadliest attack on Jewish people since the Holocaust — assault timeline, hostage crisis resolved January 2026, intelligence failures, and IDF response. On September 25, 2026 (Day 1085 / Ceasefire Day 351): The New York Times reported that Netanyahu chaired a security meeting on October 1, 2023 — six days before the attack, attended by Mossad chief David Barnea, then-defense minister Yoav Gallant, then-Shin Bet director Ronen Bar, then-IDF chief of staff Herzi Halevi, then-national security adviser Tzachi Hanegbi and then-strategic affairs minister Ron Dermer — at which Netanyahu argued for maintaining calm in Gaza to protect a potential Saudi normalization deal, overruling officials who wanted to strike Hamas figures directing West Bank attacks, and did not mention to the group the warning he had personally received from UAE President Mohammed bin Zayed roughly ten days earlier; five former senior Israeli officials told the Times the warning never reached the heads of Israel's security establishment. One day earlier, on September 24, 2026 (Day 1084 / Ceasefire Day 350): Prime Minister Netanyahu told the UN General Assembly that October 7 was 'the darkest day in Israel's history,' saying Hamas terrorists killed civilians 'with fiendish glee and sadistic joy' while livestreaming the attack, as delegates staged a walkout and protesters outside hanged a Netanyahu effigy; separately the same day, an IDF probe found the Paga Outpost ('Magen Be'eri') was unprepared for the October 7 infiltration — its combat team had never drilled for a large-scale simultaneous assault — with 22 soldiers killed, 18 wounded and two taken hostage there, opening the way for Hamas's attack on neighboring Kibbutz Be'eri; and Israel's Tekuma Directorate reported the Gaza border region's population has grown to about 66,000, roughly 10% above the pre-October 7 level, with more than 90% of evacuated residents having returned. Six days earlier, on September 18, 2026 (Day 1078 / Ceasefire Day 344): an AFP/France 24 feature reported that survivors, bereaved parents and other Israelis transformed by October 7 are running as candidates across at least nine party lists in the October 27 election — including hostage-family spokesperson Sharon Sharabi (whose brother died in Hamas captivity) on Avigdor Liberman's list, Talik Gvili (mother of a slain police officer) placed ninth on Netanyahu's Likud list, Shira Shapira (mother of Nova victim Aner Shapira, who threw back grenades to protect others) recruited by challenger Gadi Eisenkot, and retired Maj. Gen. Noam Tibon — who rallied dispersed soldiers to fight through his son's kibbutz on October 7 — on the Bennett-Lapid centrist list; the candidates are described as sharply divided between backing Netanyahu's military approach and holding him responsible for the security failure that allowed the attack. One day earlier, on September 17, 2026 (Day 1077 / Ceasefire Day 343): Hunter Biden, in an LBC radio interview with Andrew Marr, claimed Netanyahu knew in advance that Hamas was planning the October 7 attack and deliberately allowed it to proceed in order to execute an undisclosed 'plan' — without naming who else was involved or presenting evidence — while also calling the Gaza war 'akin to genocide' and saying Netanyahu has made Jews 'less safe than they've ever been since World War II.' One day earlier, on September 16, 2026 (Day 1076 / Ceasefire Day 342): the IDF and Shin Bet said they killed Jihad Samih Mahmoud Ismail, a Hamas Nukhba squad commander, in a September 11 strike in the Khan Yunis area, saying he took part in the October 7 attack on an Israeli tank crew that killed Sgt. Shaked Dahan and led to the abduction of Capt. Omer Neutra, St.-Sgt. Oz Daniel and Sgt. Nimrod Cohen, and had continued conducting ambushes against Israeli troops in violation of the ceasefire. Separately the same day, Israel's Foreign Ministry ordered every Israeli embassy worldwide to hold public October 7 commemorative events, with dedicated funding available on request, after a Haaretz investigation found diplomats at smaller missions had reported lacking budget to organize public memorial gatherings ahead of the third anniversary. One day earlier, on September 15, 2026 (Day 1075 / Ceasefire Day 341): bereaved and hostage families held a Tel Aviv press conference to release a 12-page dossier titled 'Case 7/10' (also circulated as the 'October 7 Files'), compiling 15 years of Israeli government policy and intelligence decisions they say enabled Hamas to carry out the attack — alleging Netanyahu permitted Qatari funding into Gaza and rejected a reported recommendation from then-Shin Bet chief Ronen Bar to kill Yahya Sinwar about a week before October 7; Noam Peri, daughter of hostage Chaim Peri who died in captivity, cited the disputed Haaretz UAE-warning report as further evidence Netanyahu 'didn't want to listen,' while Gil Dickmann, cousin of slain hostage Carmel Gat, called the dossier a record for 'future hostages.' The families renewed their demand that Netanyahu immediately establish a state commission of inquiry or step aside, timed six weeks before the October 27, 2026 election. One day earlier still, on September 14, 2026 (Day 1074 / Ceasefire Day 340): Haaretz reported that hostage and bereaved families — some of Israel's most visible post-October 7 political figures — have struggled to translate that visibility into a clear role within opposition parties, noting they were 'never a political monolith': most relatives pushed for ceasefire deals to bring captives home even at the cost of ending military operations, while a smaller group backed continued pressure on Hamas and aligned with the government, exemplified by hostage family member Talik Gvili's appearance at a Likud Knesset slate announcement crediting Netanyahu for the hostages' return. Three days earlier, on September 11, 2026 (Day 1071 / Ceasefire Day 337): Col. (res.) Doron Hadar, who commanded the IDF General Staff's hostage-negotiation unit from 2007 until February 2024, said mediators had warned for years before October 7 that Hamas leader Yahya Sinwar was considering a large-scale kidnapping operation to shift the group's negotiating position on a hostage-prisoner deal — warnings that never specified timing, scale or method, only that Sinwar viewed a mass-capture operation as leverage to secure Palestinian prisoners' release; Hadar said one of Hamas's central objectives on October 7 was 'to capture soldiers and civilians to get back prisoners,' adding another entry to the growing catalogue of pre-October 7 warnings — alongside the 'Jericho Wall' document, IDF Military Intelligence letters, and the disputed Haaretz report on a UAE warning to Netanyahu — that officials say were not acted on before the attack. One day earlier, on September 10, 2026 (Day 1070 / Ceasefire Day 336): the IDF and Shin Bet said they killed Ismail Ibrahim Darwish Kandil, a Hamas Nukhba operative who infiltrated Israel on October 7 and took part in killing Nahal Brigade commander Col. Yonatan Steinberg, in a strike in the Khan Younis area, saying he had recently advanced attacks on troops and civilians and worked to restore Hamas's capabilities in violation of the ceasefire; separately the same day, Netanyahu's legal team sent Haaretz a formal pre-suit warning letter over its September 8 report that UAE President Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan warned Netanyahu roughly 10 days before October 7, 2023 that Hamas was planning a major operation, and that Netanyahu never briefed Israel's security chiefs on the call; Haaretz responded the same day, saying the letter would not change its position and calling its reporting an 'in-depth, well-sourced journalistic investigation into a matter of utmost public interest,' adding it 'won't hesitate to expose the truth in court.' One day earlier, on September 9, 2026 (Day 1069 / Ceasefire Day 335): Prime Minister Netanyahu's office announced it would file a libel lawsuit against Haaretz and reporter Shlomi Eldar over the previous day's report that UAE President Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan warned him roughly 10 days before October 7, 2023 that Hamas was preparing a major operation, saying internal reviews by the Prime Minister's Office, National Security Council and military secretariat found no record of any such conversation 'from the beginning of September through October 7, 2023'; Haaretz said it stood by its report, noting three senior foreign-government representatives were said to have been informed of the call at the time. One day earlier, on September 8, 2026 (Day 1068 / Ceasefire Day 334): Haaretz reported — citing the forthcoming book 'Kidnapped: 843 Days of Abandonment' by Shlomi Eldar and Ruti Yuval — that Bin Zayed had called Netanyahu about 10 days before October 7 and, in a 45-minute conversation, warned that Hamas leader Yahya Sinwar was planning a major operation that could cause bloodshed and destabilize the region, echoing a separate 'earthquake' message Sinwar had conveyed via a Palestinian mediator; Netanyahu reacted 'relatively calmly' and briefed neither his defense minister, IDF chief of staff, nor the Shin Bet and Mossad directors on the call. His office called the report 'an absolute lie,' and opposition leaders Gadi Eisenkot, Naftali Bennett, Avigdor Liberman and Yair Golan renewed demands for a state commission of inquiry, saying 'as soon as a government under our leadership is established, we will establish a state-led commission of inquiry.' One day earlier, on September 7, 2026 (Day 1067 / Ceasefire Day 333): Defense Minister Israel Katz said he and Prime Minister Netanyahu have instructed the IDF to prepare an 'all-out war' against senior Palestinian Authority officials if security services determine the PA is launching, or about to launch, an 'October 7-style' terrorist attack from the West Bank — including targeting PA leadership, evacuating residents from attack-origin areas, and maintaining an open-ended IDF presence — a statement that followed a stabbing attack at Maoz Yehuda Farm near Kusra and IDF multi-front readiness drills including 'Dawn 2.0.' The same day, a joint Jerusalem Center for Foreign Affairs and Security (JCFA) / Lazar Research poll of 703 Israelis surveyed September 2-4 found 77% of all Israelis, and 86% of Jewish Israelis, fear a potential October 7-style attack originating from the West Bank, while 67% (75% of Jewish Israelis) oppose a Palestinian state along 1967 borders. Separately on September 7, Brig. Gen. (res.) Ofer Winter defied pressure from Netanyahu and Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich to merge with the Religious Zionist Party, submitting an independent 18-candidate 'Amcha Yisrael' Knesset slate explicitly framed around recruiting candidates 'who were not part of the events that led us to October 7'; Smotrich called the move an 'irresponsible gamble.' One day earlier, on September 6, 2026 (Day 1066 / Ceasefire Day 332): Israel's National Security Council warned that the October 2026 third anniversary of October 7 is a 'particularly sensitive period' at heightened risk of violent protests and attacks on Israelis and Jews abroad, citing Iran and its proxies as the primary threat and noting that 25 Israelis and Jews have been killed in overseas attacks since the war began. One day earlier, on September 5, 2026 (Day 1065 / Ceasefire Day 331): Channel 12 reported that Brig. Gen. (res.) Ofer Winter warned Netanyahu in the days after October 7 that an IDF Gaza ground offensive would cost roughly 15,000 soldiers' lives — a claim Winter denies and that actual losses of 473 came nowhere near; the same day, Michel Illouz, father of slain hostage Guy Illouz, told the Movement for Quality Government's Habima Square protest that a state commission of inquiry 'is not vengeance, not a tool to topple the government,' but 'a democratic country's way of saying, a disaster happened here, we need to understand why.' One day earlier, on September 4, 2026 (Day 1064 / Ceasefire Day 330): The IDF and Shin Bet said they killed Muhammad Mahmoud Marshad al-Qadi, the Hamas Nukhba commander who led the October 7 raid on Israel's Sufa military outpost and later held hostages captive in Rafah, in a strike in Khan Yunis — saying he had recently been training Hamas operatives and rebuilding the group's capabilities in violation of the ceasefire. One day earlier, on September 3, 2026 (Day 1063 / Ceasefire Day 329): Netanyahu's office published his full minute-by-minute October 7 morning timeline for the first time, showing he was alerted to the attack at 6:29 a.m. but did not speak directly with then-IDF Chief of Staff Herzi Halevi until 9:55 a.m. — nearly 3.5 hours later; the October Council called the delay 'unfathomable,' saying 'in those hours, our children, our parents, our brothers and our sisters were still alive,' while election rival Yair Golan called it 'unfathomable that Netanyahu was not in touch with Halevi' as Hamas terrorists overran towns. Two days earlier, on September 2, 2026 (Day 1062 / Ceasefire Day 328): Hundreds gathered in Skokie, Illinois for the dedication of 'Hersh's Fridge,' a kosher community fridge and memorial mural honoring Nova hostage Hersh Goldberg-Polin, murdered by Hamas in Gaza; his parents Jon Polin and Rachel Goldberg-Polin attended. One day earlier, on September 1, 2026 (Day 1061 / Ceasefire Day 327): Prime Minister Netanyahu said senior IDF and defense officials 'deliberately chose not to wake him' in the hours before October 7 out of fear that a full military alert would 'annoy Hamas' into a broader attack — then released a same-day clarifying video denying he meant 'betrayal,' saying 'I don't think there was a betrayal, I think there was a failure, a great failure.' The same day, election rival Yair Golan warned Netanyahu's wife Sara Netanyahu of a NIS 2.5 million ($825,000) defamation suit after she insinuated, in an August 31 Channel 14 interview, that his early arrival at the Nova massacre site indicated advance knowledge of the attack; Sara Netanyahu refused to apologize and threatened a NIS 1 million countersuit of her own. Israeli commentators cast the dueling statements as a coordinated Netanyahu-family effort to reframe October 7 blame ahead of the October 27 election. Two days earlier, on August 31, 2026 (Day 1060 / Ceasefire Day 326): activists from Women Demand Life protested outside the Prime Minister's Residence in Jerusalem marking two years since the bodies of the 'Beautiful Six' hostages — Hersh Goldberg-Polin, Eden Yerushalmi, Carmel Gat, Almog Sarusi, Alexander Lobanov, and Ori Danino — were recovered, accusing the government of rejecting a deal that could have brought them home alive. One day before that, on August 30, 2026 (Day 1059 / Ceasefire Day 325): organizers announced that former hostage Eli Sharabi and actress Shani Cohen will host the third grassroots national October 7 memorial ceremony at Yarkon Park, Tel Aviv on October 7, 2026, again standing in for a state ceremony that has not been held. Prior to that, on August 28, 2026 (Day 1057 / Ceasefire Day 323): Nir Oz kibbutz chairman Brig.-Gen. (res.) Tzvi 'Tzviki' Tessler said the majority of the community's roughly 400 pre-war residents still have not returned nearly three years after October 7 — in which 69 of the kibbutz's people were killed or died in captivity, about a quarter of the community and the highest per-capita toll of any single Oct. 7 site — saying many are too traumatized to return but that Nir Oz 'will prosper so that new families will come.' The IDF also confirmed strikes a day earlier, on August 27 (Day 1056 / Ceasefire Day 322), that killed Nabil Ibrahim Bass, a Hamas commander who infiltrated Israel on October 7, in Gaza's Al-Shati area, alongside Palestinian Islamic Jihad observation commander Hamdi Ahmad Hamid Kahlil in a separate Sabra-area strike, both framed by the IDF as preventing Hamas/PIJ from rebuilding in violation of the ceasefire. One day earlier still, on August 26 (Day 1055 / Ceasefire Day 321): the IDF killed Ismail Mohammed Ibrahim Barim in a Khan Younis strike — a Hamas commander who had helped hold October 7 abductee Edan Alexander, along with Matan Zangauker and Avera Mengistu, hostage in a Gaza tunnel before their releases. That followed reporting on August 27, 2026 (Day 1056 / Ceasefire Day 322): The US State Department and USAID's Office of Inspector General announced the first-ever US debarment of a terrorist affiliated with a UN humanitarian agency — Hafez Mousa Mohammed Mousa, a former UNRWA school principal who coordinated Hamas communications during the October 7 attack — and proposed debarring three more former UNRWA teachers over October 7 and Hamas/Islamic Jihad ties; Washington Free Beacon reporting citing the same USAID probe separately confirmed that Faisal Ali Al-Naami, the UNRWA 'social worker' filmed dragging slain hostage Yonatan Samerano's body into an SUV at Kibbutz Be'eri on October 7, was an active Hamas operative (he was killed in an October 2023 strike and was not himself debarred). The same day, the IDF and Shin Bet announced the killing of Razek Sahil Suleiman Abu Shahma — a former bodyguard to Yahya Sinwar — and fellow Nukhba terrorist Hazem Mousa, both of whom infiltrated the Re'im base on October 7. Three days earlier, on August 24, 2026 (Day 1053 / Ceasefire Day 319): the IDF killed Nukhba terrorist Mohammad Abd al-Nasser Jabr Abu Asaad in a Deir al-Balah strike, and the October Council, the bereaved and hostage families' advocacy group, published a report titled 'Strategic Warning: Default 2026' warning that the IDF's pre-October 7 containment mentality ('conceptzia') has persisted rather than disappeared, merely 'changed shape.' Citing IDF lookout and reservist testimony, the report says Hamas continues to rebuild, recruit, and test the ceasefire 'Yellow Line' — a leaked IDF report logged 14 violations in one 24-hour window — while field observers who raise alarms are pressured into silence. A senior security official cited in the report said Netanyahu 'received more than ten warnings' before October 7. One day earlier, on August 25, 2026 (Day 1054 / Ceasefire Day 320): Prime Minister Netanyahu ordered a UNRWA vocational training center in Kafr Aqab, East Jerusalem dismantled, saying Israel 'will not allow an organization whose employees were involved in terrorism and in the October 7 massacre to operate on its territory'; hours earlier, IDF Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir visited Gaza-border surveillance soldiers at Re'im Base and said 'one of the lessons of October 7 is that we must listen carefully to every female and male soldier,' addressing renewed complaints that spotters' warnings are again being brushed aside. Three days earlier, on August 22, roughly 250 people attended the weekly Habima Square protest, where Liad Baram — father of Nahal Oz soldier Neta Baram, killed October 7 — said the state has an 'unceasing and unforgivable debt' to investigate the failures. All of this follows the August 21 news that the IDF killed Sabahi Sami Mahmoud Shahata, a Hamas platoon commander who held Oct. 7 hostages, in an August 19 Nuseirat strike, and the August 20 release of the IDF Military Advocate-General's Corps' first war crimes report since October 7. Hamas's Al-Qassam Brigades supreme command has now been publicly vacant for more than 13 weeks since the IDF killed Mohammed Odeh on May 27; Imad Aqel remains the last identified senior October 7 planner still alive and the NILI task force's primary target. All 251 hostages accounted for as of January 26, 2026. October 7 Perpetrators Eliminated: Sinwar (Oct 16, 2024), Shambari (Apr 29, 2026), Haddad (May 16, 2026), Odeh (May 27, 2026), Khamis Ra'i (Aug 16, 2026), Shahata (Aug 19, 2026), al-Qadi (Sep 4, 2026), Kandil (Sep 10, 2026). Accountability: no state commission of inquiry established nearly three years after the attack; election set for October 27, 2026. NSC warns third Oct. 7 anniversary (Oct 2026) raises risk of overseas attacks on Israelis/Jews.
